title: US Commerce (BIS) extends AI-chip licence requirements to five 'unacceptable risk of diversion' countries and to overseas data centers serving Chinese firms; China's commerce ministry vows countermeasures; Commerce and DOJ joint statement on Megaspeed (criminal probe, DOJ lead); Nvidia reports after today's close
body:
# New US AI-chip curbs on remote access and five transit countries; China vows countermeasures; Commerce-DOJ Megaspeed statement (Nvidia reports tonight)

**1. The rule (Al Jazeera and Reuters relay via search, Nov 17; rule text not read).** Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security expanded licence requirements to five countries it calls an "unacceptable risk of diversion": Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, describing it as a "logical extension" of the existing licence requirement for chips to China-based firms. The rules also target overseas data centers that provide advanced computing capacity to Chinese companies (Al Jazeera headline: "US moves to block China's remote access to AI chips amid Nvidia scandal"). Not read by WALTER: the Federal Register or BIS text, effective date, chip thresholds, licence policy (presumption of denial or case by case).

**2. China's response.** China's commerce ministry "firmly opposed" the rule and said it would take countermeasures if the US insists on it; no measure named (Yahoo/Reuters relay; Will's bookmark @PolymarketMoney 14:59Z). Speculation that it could target critical minerals or chip raw materials is analysis only. Trump is due in Shenzhen Wed 11/18 and meets Xi Thu 11/19 (SIG-W-20261114-003).

**3. Nvidia.** CNBC (sources), Nov 17: Nvidia warned chip buyers of legal risks tied to Chinese access to AI capacity. FT and IBTimes: Nvidia created a board committee to oversee export controls, national-security policy and trade risk. ⚠️ UNVERIFIED: @PolymarketMoney (15:27Z) says Nvidia "reportedly stops selling chips to cloud firms that rent over 50% of their GPUs to Chinese companies"; WALTER found no outlet carrying a 50% threshold. Nvidia's Q3 results come after today's close (call 17:00 ET).

**4. Commerce and DOJ joint statement on Megaspeed, dated November 16, 2026** (image posted by @CommerceGov 03:31Z Nov 17, read whole by WALTER): Commerce opened an investigation into Singapore's Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export-control violations; in May 2025 Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia on direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed; in June 2025 Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its "no sell" list; BIS agents with Singaporean law enforcement did an on-site end-use check in June 2025 and interviewed CEO Alice Huang; DOJ then took the lead in the criminal investigation. The statement says it addresses "inaccurate information circulating in public reporting" and names no Nvidia wrongdoing. It also says 17 defendants in six investigations have been charged in chip-smuggling cases under this administration.

**Market context (vendor intraday 16:45Z, not closes):** NVDA 153.35 (-1.79%), S&P 500 7,311.80 (-1.41%), VIX 26.18. Card 20261116-002 (Bessent's 10-day ask to Nvidia's board on 'seemingly illicit sales') is the prior card on this thread.

title: Optimizely supply-chain compromise (Nov 16): malicious JavaScript served to 178 organizations, banking and finance hardest hit (32, incl. HSBC, Equifax), card skimming on sites' own forms, crypto-wallet swapping, iOS exploit kits; Optimizely says fixed; plus unverified outage relays (Schwab site, NSA network, DHS 'AI may be behind recent US outages'), United Airlines outage Nov 16
body:
# Optimizely supply-chain compromise: 178 organizations, 32 in banking and finance, card skimming (Nov 16)

**What is established (several security outlets via search, Nov 17: Help Net Security, The Register, Malwarebytes, cybersecuritynews; pages not opened by WALTER):** researcher Scott Helme (Report URI) found malicious JavaScript served to visitors of 178 organizations through Optimizely Web (an A/B-testing and personalisation platform); Helme checked 1,611 snippets and found 188 carrying it. The code sat in customers' "Project JavaScript" field and loaded from Optimizely's own content delivery network, so browsers trusted it. Payloads: a card skimmer on sites' own payment forms (card number, expiry, security code; third-party hosted fields such as Stripe or Adyen not exposed), crypto-wallet address swapping (about $7,000 reported to attacker wallets), cookie and screenshot theft, iOS exploit kits. Will's bookmarks (@HormuzLetter, @TheInsiderPaper): named victims include Zoom, CNN, BBC, Fox News, HSBC, Ledger, Equifax, Salesforce, IKEA, Air France-KLM; banking and finance the hardest-hit sector with 32 organizations. Optimizely says an unauthorised party exploited a flaw in its Experimentation account sign-up flow; Malwarebytes reports the flaw fixed and the code removed. Unknown: how the attacker got write access to so many unrelated projects; how many card numbers were taken; which US banks are among the 32 (CYPHER guardrail: no bank-by-bank list on the BOARD).

**Class:** bank-supplier class by effect (a vendor's code ran on 32 finance firms' customer pages and harvested payment data). WALTER sets PRIORITY: not a named core or payment-system vendor and no multi-day outage. CYPHER grades the escalation rows.

**Unverified relays, same 24 hours (Will's bookmarks, nothing found at a primary):**
- @WatcherGuru 15:30Z: "Charles Schwab's website goes down" (no outlet found).
- @disclosetv 15:38Z: NSA's classified internal network "has gone down: reports" (low-weight source).
- @Kalshi 04:37Z: "DHS Secretary says AI may be behind recent US outages" (quote and venue not found).
- @Acyn 22:10Z Nov 16, Fox: United Airlines responding to reports of a widespread system outage.
- @visegrad24: Japan's Fugaku supercomputer hacked and offline, data of about 4,600 users at risk (not verified).
- Google Threat Intelligence: attackers using LLMs to diff software updates and build exploits before patches are applied (report not read). Reuters: California sues OpenAI over its models' cyberattacks on Hugging Face and other companies.

Context: the 11/16 Chase login outage (20261116-006/-008/-010; Chase: 'not cyber-related'). Nothing here links the outages to each other or to Optimizely.
